business.Business context: This is a proposed technical design under approved requirements scope 8367e71ff015366e5c2493c11d199f3d9f7f3ad7bde902f385d10b6a5db96138. It grants no implementation, evidence disposition, milestone acceptance or execution authority.
business.Problem statement: Fresh recovery retains an Estate 1A historical checkpoint statement in 1B evidence. Existing descriptive adjudications cannot carry authenticated authority. Resolve only the exact historical relationship while retaining original evidence and conservative acceptance.
business.Objectives: Make conflicts reviewable and dispositions authenticated and durable using AEO governance; retain exact 12-root discovery and same-run checkpoints. Avoid repeated coordination instructions by exposing exact commands and persisted status.
business.User stories: An operator lists conflicts, inspects original lines and supporting hashes, records approve/reject/unresolved with rationale, then explicitly resumes the existing run once every independent gate permits it. A reviewer can reconstruct all versions and decisions after restart.
business.Functional requirements: See the registered AEO61 requirements below; technical refinements do not replace the approved scope or its two-task DAG.
business.Nonfunctional requirements: Fail closed on missing provenance/identity, unknown versions and changed evidence. Transactional append-only decision/audit persistence, deterministic hashing, race-safe duplicate handling, read-only preview and no additional scheduler or database migration.
business.Acceptance criteria: Every registered criterion must be mapped to focused tests and the established regression suite after implementation authorization. No performance target or application acceptance is introduced.

architecture.Architecture overview: Extend quality_models.py category validation and quality.py governance service with EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION version 1. Reuse GovernanceRecord, content-addressed blobs, DesignDecision, HumanVerifier/WindowsConsoleHumanVerifier and the existing transaction/audit infrastructure. recovery_discovery.py classifies relationships after the provenance validator supplies an applicable disposition; autonomous_services.py coordinates fresh collection and existing RECONCILING checkpoints. The CLI remains the human entry point.
architecture.Impacted microservices: Only agrosphere-orchestrator code is in scope. All 12 configured application repositories remain read-only evidence sources. No application service, UI, provider, merge, publication or deployment change.
architecture.DDD boundaries: EvidenceObservation is a captured fact. EvidenceRelationship identifies a contradiction or historical reference between exact observations and affected milestones. EvidenceDisposition is authority over that relationship only. Milestone acceptance, design approval, plan approval, execution grant, quality policy and delivery approval retain their existing guards.
architecture.APIs and event interactions: Proposed evidence list/inspect/request/decide CLI delegates to existing governance services. EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION uses category-specific context independent of active delivery quality policy: discovery conflicts occur before delivery readiness. Existing delivery categories keep their current active_policy/context validation unchanged. No API server or external event bus is added.
architecture.Database changes: No migration or new table. Store versioned canonical subject as an existing immutable content-addressed blob; append approval.request and disposition audit GovernanceRecords, and governance.EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION DesignDecisions. Reuse the existing transaction and writer serialization/sequence guarantees; a duplicate lookup and append occur inside one serialized transaction. No updates to old decisions, original snapshots or audit rows. Unsupported versions are readable as opaque history and inapplicable for authority.
architecture.Security considerations: Governance SID authorization is separate from design/execution lists. Empty governance list denies all decisions. Validate the exact decision+rationale+subject digest during human confirmation; re-read settings, evidence hashes, manifest, policy version and request state after authentication inside the transaction. Reject agent/self-approval, symlink/path escape, unknown roots, missing provenance and forged outcome metadata. Local database/config administrators remain trusted operators under existing assumptions.
architecture.Technology decisions: Use existing Python/Pydantic strict models, SQLAlchemy records and Windows verifier. Canonical JSON uses sorted keys, fixed schema version, stable field ordering through canonical serialization and SHA-256 UTF-8. Paths are normalized repository-relative POSIX names; retain case-sensitive original identity and validate resolved containment. No timestamp-based winner selection.
architecture.Architectural trade-offs: Use immutable category-specific blobs rather than SQL columns to avoid migrations and preserve old consumers. Review results can be reapplied as reference dispositions, not consumed one-time execution grants; keep current one-time semantics for all other governance categories. Recollect after restart instead of trusting cached reports. The price is conservative re-review on any bound input change.
architecture.Risks and assumptions: The existing run is expired, governance/execution SIDs and approved roadmap are unconfigured. Adjudication does not remove these blockers. Rendering can use the already present local PlantUML JAR with process-scoped configuration. Rule review cannot establish conceptual correctness; authenticated human design review remains mandatory.
architecture.Architectural decisions: ADR61-1: use existing governance store and authentication. ADR61-2: only an exact relationship can become non-blocking. ADR61-3: approve/reject/unresolved are immutable decisions; revocation is a later explicit event and never deletion. ADR61-4: no migration, deadline extension, watcher or application execution in this scope. ADR61-5: original approval-bound documents remain frozen; current operations guidance is versioned with this design package.
architecture.Integration design: collect exact manifest roots -> build immutable relationship candidates -> load category-specific requests/decisions -> recompute applicability -> run existing classifier with validated relationship overlay -> persist a new recovery snapshot through existing reconciliation only when the controller runs. Approval does not rewrite previous snapshots. RECONCILING exposes request ID, subject, review path and human command. Unrelated contradictions and missing acceptance still block.

service.Technical design:
The subject schema is EvidenceDispositionSubjectV1: version=1; project; exact sorted affected_milestones; relationship_type=historical-reference; source and referenced observations; original and supporting references; proposed_effect=non-blocking-historical-observation; manifest byte SHA-256 plus canonical resolved root/id mapping digest; classifier_version; disposition_policy_version/digest; stable observation_digest. Each evidence reference contains repository ID, repo-relative path, whole-file SHA-256, line start/end, excerpt hash, observed HEAD, origin commit when independently known or explicit null with reason, and evidence kind (original/report quotation/fixture). Record captured_at in the request envelope, outside identity, so repeated identical collection is idempotent. A missing origin commit may be explicitly known-missing without inventing it; missing current file/hash/line, uncertain source relationship or ambiguous origin mapping makes approval inapplicable. Preserve captured content in the existing immutable blob so history remains inspectable after files change.

Applicability requires exact manifest/root mapping, evidence bytes/lines, observation identity, policy/version, current authorized SID, unexpired request and latest eligible decision. No record is authoritative merely because it includes disposition fields. An approved historical-reference allows only the named relationship to stop contributing a conflict; it does not suppress all claims in a document, other milestone evidence, or acceptance checks. Changed evidence invalidates that applicability; old records remain visible.
service.Domain model:
Request identity = SHA-256(canonical(subject)); use action evidence-disposition:<subject digest>. Store requesting actor separately from authorized deciding SID. A decision contains request ID, subject digest, disposition, rationale, supporting-reference digests, authenticated actor SID, timestamp, manifest/policy/classifier versions and correlation/run IDs for audit only. The same evidence relationship is reusable across reports; the run ID is not a substitute for evidence identity.

Decision state: pending -> approved | rejected | unresolved. Proposed CLI unresolved maps to an explicit immutable decision value scoped to governance.EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION only. Reject and unresolved both retain the checkpoint; unresolved means request more evidence, not approval. A terminal identical decision returns its existing ID only when every authenticated field matches; conflicting repeat is denied. Rejection/unresolved cannot be superseded by renewing expiry or changing only rationale/timestamp/requester. New substantive provenance/evidence or policy version is necessary for a revised subject. Approved -> revoked appends a revocation; revocation is sticky for that subject. Revocation is permitted after request expiry to preserve audit intent, but no expired request can grant authority. Every evaluation checks current authority and expiry.
service.Interfaces:
Proposed commands (unavailable until implementation): evidence list --run <run>; evidence inspect <request-id>; evidence request --run <run> --milestone 1B --subject <reviewed-subject.json> --reason <text> --expires-seconds <bounded>; evidence decide <request-id> --disposition approved|rejected|unresolved|revoked --reason <text>. Listing/inspection are read-only; requesting creates no authority and cannot decide. Derive the request subject from fresh exact-root discovery and validate any submitted file matches it; never trust arbitrary JSON to assert provenance. Reuse existing 1..86400 second request bounds, default 900, without extending decision validity. Print the precise confirmation subject including request/subject/disposition/rationale digest and full review details before Windows authentication. No actor flag, password argument or noninteractive approval mode.

Extend approvals inspect/pending so this category is visible. Existing approvals decide routes this category through the same validator and cannot bypass exact rationale/disposition confirmation; other categories remain compatible. Proposed interfaces are design commitments only; no command is claimed operational.
service.Persistence:
Reuse GovernanceRecord append-only request/decision/revocation/application-reference events and existing blob() integrity checks. Reuse DesignDecision(kind=governance.EVIDENCE_DISPOSITION,subject=request.id), not design requirements/design decisions. Record decision and audit in one transaction; no parallel evidence store. Before insertion acquire the established serialized writer transaction, requery identical requests/final decisions and check fresh context. Concurrent identical requests converge to one request; competing final decisions allow one and reject the other. On rollback neither decision nor audit persists. Verify SQLite transaction behavior in concurrency tests; do not assume an ordinary deferred read transaction serializes duplicate checks.

Restart reconstructs state from immutable records, recomputes evidence applicability and recollects exactly the 12 application roots. Original report, snapshot, run request/limits, counters and prior approvals are never changed. Snapshot disposition metadata is explanatory, not independently trusted. Legacy snapshots lacking versioned metadata retain conservative classification. No Alembic change; migration version and existing rows must remain identical.
service.Security: Use WindowsConsoleHumanVerifier for exact subject and decision; bind rationale digest into its subject as well. Before prompting and again before transactional commit, read current Settings governance SID allowlist and category policy; reject any removed actor, requesting actor or noncanonical SID. Revalidate bytes/root containment after authentication and before classification; classifier authority is computed from a single fresh captured observation set, never supplied by exported text. Record a distinct structured invalidation reason on changed input; do not mutate past decisions. Approval of this design is not an evidence decision.
service.Developer documentation:
Preserve the registered DAG: adjudication-integration (developer/code-write), then verification (qa-engineer/validate). Serial documentation roles are business-analyst, solution-architect, technical-writer through the existing generate_design adapter; rule architecture reviewer is a deterministic check, not a spawned agent or human approval. After design approval use milestone implementation-ready, milestone plan/approve-plan, milestone prepare and exact agent execution grants according to the existing CLI and reports; do not run them now.

Focused security/regression matrix: approve/reject/unresolved/revoke; empty/removed/unauthorized/self SID; rationale/disposition swap during prompt; changed evidence/manifest/HEAD/root and line; explicit known-missing commit versus ambiguous provenance; fixture/export quotation cross-repo identity; duplicate requests and simultaneous conflicting decisions; TTL rollover, sticky negative outcomes and unknown versions; rollback audit atomicity; restart re-collection; exact historical 1A/1B relationship with an unrelated contradiction retained; no accepted/completed promotion; same-run checkpoint recovery with original request, deadline and budgets preserved; 12-root restriction; default legacy governance behavior. Use disposable databases/Git fixtures for decision and concurrency tests, identify verifier mocks clearly. Run focused suites, then .venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/validate.py after authorized source changes. Capture raw exits and preserve prior validation reports. No live model/provider, application benchmark or build is implied.

overview.Milestone overview: This is a proposed technical design under approved requirements scope 8367e71ff015366e5c2493c11d199f3d9f7f3ad7bde902f385d10b6a5db96138. It grants no implementation, evidence disposition, milestone acceptance or execution authority.
overview.What will be built: Versioned evidence-disposition subjects and category-specific existing-governance validation, exact human CLI review, recovery relationship integration and actionable controller checkpoints.
overview.Why it is needed: The original evidence remains valid historical context but currently blocks discovery without an authenticated way to establish its exact relationship.
overview.Platform fit: AEO-1 through AEO-6 services, durable run and registered task DAG remain the orchestration system. No new run, scheduler, approval framework or watcher.
overview.Component responsibilities: Governance owns authenticated decisions; discovery owns observed provenance; classifier owns conservative relationships; controller owns bounded continuation; humans retain product and approval decisions.
overview.Implementation sequence: Requirements approval verified. Generate and validate this revision, then stop for authenticated design approval. Later implementation-ready/plan/exact execution grants must independently pass; the developer task precedes the QA task.
overview.Expected outcomes: Approved dispositions can remove only their exact relationship conflicts. Milestone 1B remains PARTIAL without fresh acceptance. Milestone 2 product/performance gates, roadmap and expiry remain independent.
overview.User-facing documentation: The versioned AUTONOMOUS_OPERATIONS_GUIDE.md in this review package lists available CLI commands and distinguishes proposed evidence commands. Operator approval is followed by explicit autonomous resume only once every independent blocker is resolved. No automatic restart currently exists.

diagrams.adjudication-state:
@startuml
title AEO-6.1 disposition applicability
state "Unresolved evidence" as Unresolved
state "Pending authenticated review" as Review
state "Approved exact relationship" as Scoped
state "Rejected" as Rejected
state "More evidence required" as More
state "Revoked or stale" as Invalid
Unresolved --> Review : Canonical versioned subject
Review --> Scoped : Authorized approved decision
Review --> Rejected : Authorized rejected decision
Review --> More : Authorized unresolved decision
Scoped --> Invalid : Revoked, expired, changed evidence or authority
Rejected --> Unresolved : Still blocking
More --> Unresolved : Still blocking
Invalid --> Unresolved : Still blocking
note right of Scoped
No milestone acceptance transition
All independent gates remain
end note
@enduml

CLI -> Discovery : Recollect manifest-bound evidence

Verifier -> Governance : Canonical authenticated SID
Governance -> Discovery : Recheck current evidence and policy

Governance -> Controller : Scoped result or blocking reason
